articles.titre: China factory output slows to 4.8% in October, retail sales up just 0.4% as demand sags
articles.resume: The data pushes in two directions for markets. Weak domestic demand and the investment slump support the case for more easing over time. But the view that no new stimulus will come this year limits any near-term “bad news is good news” rally in Chinese equities. The muted yuan reaction suggests the miss was largely expected. For commodities, slower factory output and the property slump are a headwind for iron ore and industrial metals. Softer Chinese activity also adds a mild drag on oil demand, against a supply backdrop still dominated by the Iran war. The Australian dollar is the most direct FX proxy for China, and could underperform if risk appetite weakens. --- Earlier: China’s October d

articles.titre: Japan economy shrinks 0.1% in Q3, first fall in 4 quarters as inflation hits households
articles.resume: The pushback from economists matters more for markets than the headline miss. If weak consumption is read as a sign of inflation rather than a reason to pause, December hike pricing should hold. That limits any lasting yen weakness from the data, although USD/JPY near 160 remains in intervention territory. The risk lies in the board split some economists flagged. Further soft consumption data could give the doves more influence and push hike timing back, which would weigh on the yen and lift JGBs. Oil is the link in the middle. Energy-driven inflation is both hurting households and pushing the BOJ to tighten, so higher crude makes the policy dilemma worse. --- Earlier: Japan Q3 GDP shrinks 0

articles.titre: China’s October data shows the economy losing momentum on retail sales and industry output
articles.resume: China October activity data China’s October data shows the economy losing momentum on both fronts. Industrial output growth slowed to 4.8%, missing the 5.3% forecast and down from 5.5% in September. That is notable because factories have been the main source of strength this year, helped by exports of AI-related technology. The slowdown came despite a soft comparison with last October, which points to cooling momentum rather than base effects.Retail sales were weaker still, rising just 0.4% against expectations of 0.8%, which matches August’s subdued pace. articles.titre: Japan Q3 GDP shrinks 0.1% annualised vs +0.3% expected as exports and consumers weigh
articles.resume: A flat quarter made weak mainly by trade is unlikely to derail BoJ tightening plans by itself. Strong capex and positive domestic demand are the parts policymakers watch most closely. The miss still gives the yen little help just as USD/JPY presses toward 160, and that raises the stakes for any comments from Japanese officials on the currency. JGB yields may ease slightly at the front end if traders trim December hike bets. The bigger driver for the session is Takata’s speech later today, where a hawkish response to the data would quickly restore conviction. articles.titre: Trump out of public view since Wednesday, fuelling speculation on his wherabouts
articles.resume: For markets, this is a non-event as long as the official record keeps showing normal activity. Traders have learned to discount social media speculation about the president’s health, and nothing so far has moved oil, Treasuries or the US dollar on this story. The risk lies in his travel plans. A smooth departure for China would close the story, but an unexplained delay or cancellation would quickly become a factor for markets. articles.titre: New Zealand services PSI hits 3.5-year high at 51.7, fifth straight month of growth
articles.resume: A services reading at a multi-year high, led by new orders, strengthens the case that New Zealand’s recovery is spreading beyond a handful of sectors. That gives the New Zealand dollar modest support on the domestic data front. For rate expectations, firmer activity reduces the pressure for further policy support. The flat employment reading and persistent cost-of-living complaints, however, point to slack that has not yet closed.
